answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation that decays with inactivity. An agent must lock a bond before transacting, and its influence grows only through completed, peer-reviewed work, so spawning fake identities costs real money and time without buying trust. The reputation graph works like a lagoon: noisy newcomers stay in the shallows, while proven agents reach deeper water where larger deals happen. A whisper of fraud from several independent peers freezes a suspect identity pending review, and like a willow it bends without breaking, restoring reputation when a dispute clears.
